sources.section: N5, N4 and N3 listening descriptors
sources.supports: N4 generally follows slowly spoken everyday conversations; N5 emphasizes necessary information in short slowly spoken conversations; near-natural speed appears in N3.
sources.limits: No per-dialogue duration, TTS setting, WPM or exhaustive vocabulary/grammar list.

sources.supports: Four separate listening objectives: appropriate action, a previously specified point, an expression fitting an illustrated circumstance, and a response to a short utterance. Listening approximately 35 minutes.

sources.countInspection: Section boundaries and terminal question numbers inspected throughout the 12-page extracted script.
supports: Observed scored counts 8/7/5/8 and separate worked examples.
Polite and familiar speech, reference across turns, corrected constraints, participant roles, event stages and conversational response fit.
Focused question/passage/repeated question and numbered spoken alternatives.
sources.limits: Sample observations, not a guaranteed current item count. No fresh perceptual audio audition or exhaustive linguistic audit. No official script, image or recording is republished.

sources.supports: Approximately 35 minutes for N4 listening, 30 for N5; times may vary with recordings. N4 has no separate general-outline or integrated-comprehension listening item type.

sources.section: Why current Test Content Specifications are not published
sources.supports: No exhaustive current published vocabulary, kanji and grammar syllabus; communicative task performance matters alongside language knowledge.

sources.section: What is the JLPT Can-do Self-Evaluation List
sources.supports: Self-evaluation survey evidence, explicitly not the test syllabus or guaranteed proficiency.
Starter through Elementary 2 supports N4 preparation, but Irodori levels do not directly map to JLPT levels and it is not an exam-preparation textbook.
